B.N. Chowdhury with Mahmudul Islam ------ For the Petitioner.

Radha Kanta Banik ------ Petitioner.
vs.
The Deputy Commissioner of Rangpur and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Abdur Rahman Chowdhury, J-The application under Article 102 of the Constitution of Bangladesh is directed easiest order passed by the Deputy Commissioner, Rangpur under the Requisition of Property Acts 1948. The case it appears, had a checkered career. Facts leading to this rule in brief are that the petitioner was a businessman of Rangpur and his property was requisitioned under the Requisition of Property Act, 1948 (hereinafter called the Act ) on 10/9/65 and possession was also taken over on the same day. On 8-9-65. i.e. 2 days before the property was requisitioned the petitioner was taken into custody under the Defence of Pakistan Rules and was kept under detention till 10-7-66. On 30-9-65 the Deputy Commissioner again passed an order of requisition in respect of the self-same properties plus 11 acres of land belonging to the petitioner and allotted the same to M/s Ashish Corporation and delivered possession to the said Corporation on 18-11-65. Thereafter an order of acquisition was passed on 9-7-66 and same was published in the official gazette on 21-7-66. The petitioner on being released from detention on 10.7.66 filed a revisional application for vacating the order of requisition and on for the release of his property which was however rejected by the Government. The petitioner thereafter moved the then High Court of East Pakistan by writ petition No. 27 of 1967 for a declaration that the impugned orders of requisition and acquisition were without lawful authority but the High Court by judgment dated 24-6-68 dismissed the writ petition against which judgment the petitioner preferred Civil Appeal No. 63-D of 1968 before the erst-while Supreme Court of Pakistan. On 3-7-69 the Supreme Court of Pakistan set aside the judgment of the High Court and declared the impugned orders of requisition and acquisition as being without lawful authority and of no legal effect (Annexure C), Par snout to taken Judgment passed by Supreme Court, the Deputy Commissioner of Rangpur by his order dated 23-2-70 directed the allotted (respondent No. 4) to surrender possession of the said properties to the Land Acquisition Officer by 25-3-70 (Annexure D). Thereafter, the Government of East Pakistan filed an application for review of the judgment dated 3-7-69 before the Supreme Court with a prayer for stay of operation of the judgment. The prayer for, stay was, however, rejected by the Supreme Court on 6-4-70 (Annexure D-I ) In the meanwhile, on 24-3-70 respondent No. 4 ( hereinafter called the respondent ) as plaintiff fired other Suit No. 16 of 1970 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Rangpur against the Government of East Pakistan and others for a declaration that the respondent) had the right to possess the suit properties and the order of the Deputy Commissioner dated 23-2-70 directing him to surrender the property was illegal and without jurisdiction and also for permanent in-junction restraining the defendant (The Deputy Commissioner, Rangpur) from taking over possession of the aforesaid property from the respondent. It is interesting to note that the petitioner was rot made a party in the said suit. On the prayer of the plaintiff respondent temporary injunction was granted restraining the defendant (represent No. 1) froth disturbing the possession of the plaintiff in the suit property. The suit, however, was dismissed on contest by judgment dated 27-12-71 (Annexure). The respondent there after filed other Appeal No. 2 of 1972 against the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge but on 2-9-72 on the application of the Government the detect District Judge recorded abatement of the said appeal under article (42) of President Order No. 69 of 1972. The respondent thereafter as pettier moved this Court under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure being Civil Revision No. 758 of 1972 and the Court by its judgment dated 2-8-73 discharged the rule on contest ( Annexure 2 ) against which the respondent as appellant filed Civil Appeal No. 23 of 1973 before the Appellate Division of this Court and on his prayer the Appellate Division, by order dated 22-10-73, restrained the Government of Bangladesh from disturbing the possession of the appellant (respondent No. 4 ) in the suit property. It appears that the application filed for review of the judgment of the erstwhile Supreme Court of Pakistan was dismissed by the Appellate Division at the instance of the Government of Bangladesh not pressed. An application for Vacation of the aforesaid order of ad interim injunction passed by the Appellate Division was also filed by the Government of Bangladesh on the ground that the respondent had no interest in the property and that he was pursuing the matter of malafide only to defeat the ends of justice and further that the lawful owner of the property was being illegally kept out of possession for more than 9 years causing irreparable loss to him and the Government was under legal and moral obligation to hand over possession of the property to the rightful owner, namely the petitioner. The Appellate Division, by order dated 18-3-77 vacated the ad interim order passed on 22-10-73 (Annexure F). Thereafter the petitioner tiled an application before the Deputy. Commissioner, Rangpur (Respondent No, 1) praying for restoration of possession of his properties against which the respondent filed an objection. After hearing the parties the Deputy Commissioner, Rangpur responders No. 1) passed the impugned order dated 15-3-78 directing the petitioner to move the Civil Court for restoration of possession of his properties (Annexure I) against which order the petitioner moved this Court obtained the present rule. 

 9. In view or the foregoing discussions we are firmly of the view that the only duty of the Deputy Commissioner was to implement the order dated 23.2.70 which was rightly passed by his predecessor and the validity and legality of the said order was also upheld and affirmed by the learned Subordinate Judge while dismissing the civil suit instituted by the respondent. Thereafter, the Appellate Division of this court having vacated the ad interim injunction by order dated 18th March, 1977 there was not only a civil court decree upholding the Deputy Commissioner's order but there was also no legal impediment or restraint upon him to carry out and implement the aforesaid order. It was the legal and constitutional obligation on the part of the Deputy Commissioner to implement and enforce the judgment of the erstwhile Supreme Court of Pakistan.
